name: Reconcile AESO power pool settlement statements
summary: Every month the Alberta Electric System Operator (AESO) settles the wholesale power pool: it posts a preliminary statement for each pool participant on the fifth business day, a final statement on the fifteenth, and moves the money by wire on the twentieth. A settlement analyst rebuilds each statement hour by hour from the company's own meter, dispatch, offer and trade records, chases differences with the AESO or the meter data manager, and books the result. The work is slow because statements hold thousands of asset-hours, the preliminary-to-final window is only ten business days, and each production month is resettled again at two and four months, so differences surface long after the month closed.

baseline.org_archetype: An Alberta merchant generator with gas, hydro, wind and battery assets held in several pool participant entities and a central settlement team in its energy marketing division.
baseline.notes: Statement counts assume four pool participant entities (as TransAlta had in the MSA's 2021 penalty table: TransAlta Generation Partnership, TA Alberta Hydro LP, TransAlta Corporation, Canadian Hydro Developers) with a preliminary and a final statement each, plus partner-unit and transmission-related statements.

trigger: The AESO posts a preliminary or final power pool statement for one of the company's pool participant entities in the Energy Trading System.
end_state: A preliminary statement has been reconciled and every material difference queried before the final; or a final statement has been tied out, disputed if needed, paid or received on the 20th business day and posted to the ledger.

volume.seasonality: Statement count is fixed by the settlement calendar; the work per statement rises in months with extreme pool prices (for example the February 2021 cold snap and summer 2021 heat) because uplift, dispatch-down and restatement lines grow.

evidence.note: Two statements (preliminary and final) per participant per month from the guide; four TransAlta pool participant entities appear in the MSA 2021 penalty tables; count of other statements is the author's estimate.

Organisation file role. FTE is the author's estimate: per-statement work plus the daily review of ETS settlement reports the AESO recommends during the month, which is not modelled as steps. Loaded cost per hour copied from the organisation file (wage x 1.40: benefits about 25 percent, overhead about 15 percent).

systems.name: AESO Energy Trading System (offers, declarations and dispatch)
Energy trading and risk management system
ERP (finance, purchasing and plant maintenance modules)

steps.name: Post statement in the Energy Trading System
steps.description: The AESO posts a preliminary power pool statement by the end of the fifth business day after the production month, or a final statement by the end of the fifteenth, for one pool participant, and sends a message in the Energy Trading System that it is ready.

evidence.note: Posting days and ETS message from the settlement guide.

steps.name: Log statement and download supporting reports
steps.description: The settlement analyst logs into the Energy Trading System with the company's digital certificate, downloads the statement and the csv reports behind it (daily detail, metered volumes, NSI detail, trading charge, settlement changes, PFAM summary) and records the statement in the monthly settlement tracker.

evidence.note: Report names and locations from section 3.4 and Appendix 1 of the settlement guide; times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Load statement data into the shadow settlement
steps.description: The analyst imports the hourly csv data into the shadow settlement workbook, maps each AESO pool asset ID to the plant, hydro group or wind farm and legal entity, and refreshes the hourly pool price so every line can be recomputed independently.

error.defect_description: An asset ID is mapped to the wrong plant or entity, or a pasted range is short by some hours.

evidence.note: Shadow settlement in spreadsheets or the ETRM settlement module was common practice for Alberta pool participants; times estimated.

steps.name: Compare metered volumes with plant records
steps.description: The analyst compares the AESO metered energy for each asset and hour with the plant historian's net-to-grid MWh and the dispatch log, and flags hours where the gap exceeds the tolerance, such as a missing hour after a meter or communications fault.

error.defect_description: A small but real meter gap is accepted as within tolerance.

evidence.note: The guide says metered volume reports post five business days after production and that generators should check with their meter data manager; comparison method and times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Recompute energy payments and market charges
steps.description: For each asset and hour the analyst recomputes the energy payment as volume times pool price, applies the energy market trading charge rate, and checks payments to a supplier on the margin, transmission constraint rebalancing and dispatch down service lines against the offer and dispatch records.

evidence.note: Line items listed in section 3.3 of the settlement guide; recalculation times estimated.

steps.name: Reconcile net settlement instructions with bilateral trades
steps.description: The analyst compares the net settlement instructions accepted in the Energy Trading System, hour by hour, with the physical bilateral power trades booked in the ETRM system, because each instruction moves volume between participants and changes the energy payment.

evidence.note: NSI and meter volume breakdown and NSI detail reports described in the settlement guide (ISO rule 103.5); times estimated.

steps.name: Check operating reserve payments and fees
steps.description: The analyst compares operating reserve payments and charges with the ancillary service awards and delivery records, and checks the other lines on the statement such as the participation fee, interest on late payments and cash on deposit.

evidence.note: Fees and interest lines are in the settlement guide; how operating reserve settlement lines are presented was not confirmed in an opened source, so the check is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Review prior period resettlement lines
steps.description: The analyst reviews the prior period energy and charge lines, which carry the interim (two month) and final (four month) resettlements of earlier production months, and ties each change to earlier shadow figures and to queries still open in the tracker.

evidence.note: Initial, interim and final settlement runs at one, two and four months from section 5.1(d) of the guide.

steps.name: Summarise variances and apply materiality
steps.description: The analyst totals the variances from the metering, energy, NSI, ancillary and prior period checks by cause in the variance log, applies the department's dollar and MWh materiality thresholds, and decides which items need follow-up before the next statement.

error.defect_description: An item is classed as immaterial that should have been queried.

evidence.note: Share of statements with a material variance is the author's estimate for a multi-asset fleet.

steps.name: Investigate the cause of a material variance
steps.description: The analyst pulls historian trends and dispatch logs, asks the real-time desk or the plant control room about curtailments, derates or meter work, and checks the shadow settlement mapping to decide whether the error lies with the company, the meter data or the AESO calculation.

next.condition: error in the shadow settlement, corrected and re-summarised
AESO data or calculation appears wrong

evidence.note: Split of root causes estimated by the author.

steps.name: Meter data manager confirms and resubmits meter data
steps.description: The company's meter data manager checks whether all generation data reached the AESO and, where data were missing or wrong, resubmits corrected interval data so that the correction appears on the final statement or a later resettlement.

evidence.note: The guide directs generators with production discrepancies to their meter data manager; turnaround estimated.

steps.name: Send a settlement query to the AESO
steps.description: The analyst emails settlement@aeso.ca with the day, hour ending, pool asset, MWh or dollar amount according to company records and supporting extracts, and logs the query with its expected correction date in the tracker.

evidence.note: Query address and the information the AESO asks for come from section 5.1 of the guide; times estimated.

steps.name: AESO processes the correction or answers the query
steps.description: AESO settlement staff review the query or the resubmitted meter data and either correct the final statement, schedule the change for the next resettlement run, or reply explaining why the figure stands.

evidence.note: AESO response time estimated; the guide encourages queries before the final statement is issued ten business days after the preliminary.

steps.name: Manager reviews the reconciliation package
steps.description: The manager of settlement and contracts reviews the variance log, open queries and the tie of statement totals to the shadow settlement, signs off the preliminary review or releases the final statement for payment, and returns the work if a variance is unexplained.

control.basis: Internal control over financial reporting (NI 52-109 certification and SOX 404 for a US-listed issuer): independent review of revenue reconciliations

next.condition: preliminary statement reviewed; queries raised before the final

evidence.note: Roughly half of the statements are preliminary and half final; review times estimated.

steps.name: Compare the final statement with the preliminary and open queries
steps.description: The analyst checks that the corrections agreed with the AESO or the meter data manager appear on the final statement, ties the final total to the shadow settlement, and decides whether any remaining difference is large enough to dispute.

next.condition: final agrees or remaining difference is immaterial

evidence.note: Final statements include corrections to preliminary statements (section 3.2 of the guide); dispute share estimated.

steps.name: Draft a written settlement dispute
steps.description: The analyst drafts a formal written dispute with hourly calculations and evidence, has the manager sign it, and files it with the AESO before the twenty-business-day dispute submission period after the final energy market statement closes.

control.basis: ISO rules section 103.2 (Dispute Resolution) and section 103.4 subsection 27: written dispute within the published dispute submission period

evidence.note: Dispute rule and twenty-business-day window from the guide and the AESO dispute timeline.

steps.name: Approve the net amount to pay or receive
steps.description: The manager approves the net amount on the final statement to be paid to or received from the AESO, noting that the full amount must be paid even while a dispute is open, and sends the payment approval to treasury.

control.basis: Treasury and payments policy: settlement approves the amount, treasury releases the wire

evidence.note: Full payment despite a dispute and payment by wire from sections 4 and 5.2 of the guide.

steps.name: Release the wire or confirm the receipt
steps.description: On the twentieth business day the treasury analyst releases the wire transfer to the AESO's account for a net payable statement, or confirms that the AESO's wire arrived for a net receivable one, and records the bank reference.

control.basis: ISO rules section 103.4 subsections 20 and 23: settlement on the 20th business day by wire transfer

evidence.note: Wire-only payment on the 20th business day from section 4 of the guide; wait is the gap from final approval to that date.

steps.name: Prepare and post the settlement journal entries
steps.description: The analyst reverses the month-end accrual made from the shadow settlement, books final energy revenue, ancillary revenue, fees and prior period adjustments by asset and legal entity, and uploads the journal for the accounting team's month-end close.

error.defect_description: An adjustment is posted to the wrong entity or period.

control.basis: Internal control over financial reporting: documented support and review of revenue journal entries

evidence.note: Journal practice estimated for a listed generator.

steps.name: Update the query log and resettlement watchlist
steps.description: The analyst closes resolved queries in the tracker and carries open items and expected corrections forward to the watchlist for the interim and final resettlement runs that will appear on later statements.

evidence.note: Tracking practice estimated.

exceptions.name: Missing meter data
exceptions.description: A meter or communications fault leaves hours missing; the meter data manager resubmits and the correction lands on the final statement or a later resettlement.

exceptions.name: AESO calculation or NSI error
exceptions.description: An uplift, net settlement instruction or prior period line disagrees with company records; the analyst queries the AESO and tracks the correction.

exceptions.name: Formal dispute
exceptions.description: A material difference remains on the final statement; the company pays in full and files a written dispute within twenty business days.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from statement posting to reconciliation sign-off (preliminary) or posting of journal entries (final)
benchmarks.population: Preliminary and final power pool statements of an Alberta pool participant

evidence.note: Derived from the settlement calendar: ten business days (about 14 calendar days) between preliminary and final statements cap the preliminary review, and five business days (about 7 calendar days) separate the final statement from payment, followed by journal posting.

benchmarks.unit: business days after the end of the settlement period
benchmarks.population: AESO power pool financial settlement under ISO rule 103.4

benchmarks.unit: business days after the final energy market statement

pain_points.description: Each statement holds hourly data for dozens of assets, and the shadow settlement is rebuilt in spreadsheets each month, so most of the analyst's time goes to re-keying and matching rather than investigating.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice.

pain_points.description: Only ten business days separate the preliminary and final statements, so queries raised late slip to the interim or final resettlement two to four months later.

evidence.note: Statement timing from the guide; the consequence is the author's inference.

pain_points.description: Each production month is resettled at one, two and four months and the final energy market statement issues about five months after the period, so open items must be tracked across many statements.

assumptions: The unit of work is one statement. Preliminary statements end at the manager's sign-off with queries raised; final statements continue to payment and posting. The split is modelled at the manager review step (s14) because the statement type is known at posting.

Settlement analysts also review ETS settlement reports during the month, as the AESO recommends, and book a month-end accrual from the shadow settlement before statements arrive; that work is counted in the analyst FTE but not modelled as steps.
No surge is given: statement volume is fixed by the AESO calendar, and price spikes raise the work per statement rather than the number of statements.
No physical resources, travel or field wait causes apply to this office process.
Treasury releases the wire; the organisation file lists only settlement roles for this process.
Times and branch shares are tier C estimates unless a step cites a source; the AESO dates are tier A or B.

sources.title: Information Document: Power Pool Settlement Guide, ID #2011-002R
sources.supports: Preliminary power pool statements by the end of the 5th business day after the settlement period and final statements by the 15th; payments based on final statements and settled by wire on the 20th business day; statement line items (energy payment, trading charge, PSM, TCR, dispatch down service, prior period adjustments, participation fee, interest); verification reports in the Energy Trading System (metered volumes updated 5 business days after production, NSI reports, settlement changes, PFAM summary); generator discrepancies go to the meter data manager, other queries to settlement@aeso.ca; each production month settled at 1 month (initial), 2 months (interim) and 4 months (final); written disputes on final statements under section 103.2; final amount must be paid in full despite a dispute.

sources.title: Power Pool Financial Settlement 2020-2021 Dispute Timelines
sources.supports: Issue dates of the final energy market statement for August 2020 to December 2021 settlement periods (about five months after each period, for example Aug 2020 final issued Jan 22, 2021) and the dispute submission period of twenty business days after that issue date; initial, interim and final runs at one, two and four months.

sources.title: MSA Compliance Review 2021
sources.supports: 462 ISO rules matters addressed in 2021 (437 in 2020), 91 percent self-reported; outcomes 341 forbearance, 75 notices of specified penalty, 44 no contravention; 56 matters unresolved at end of 2021; 10 percent of self-reported and 77 percent of AESO-referred matters received a specified penalty; most matters under sections 203.3 (restatements), 203.4, 201.7, 205.5 and 205.6; TransAlta Generation Partnership 8 penalty matters (19,500 CAD), TA Alberta Hydro LP 5 (8,000 CAD), TransAlta Corporation 1 (500 CAD) and TransAlta Generation Partnership 1 O&P ARS matter (2,250 CAD); 80 O&P ARS and 294 CIP ARS matters addressed; O&P ARS counts vary with the three-year audit cycle; no penalty disputed.
